raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` checkpoint keeps the q_a, kv_a, q_b, and o attention projections in BF16. They are represented by three modules: `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, and `o_proj`.

This PR adds a default-off PTPC FP8 path on gfx950 using per-token activation scales and per-channel weight scales. BF16 remains the default and fallback.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_DSA_FP8_PROJ_GEMM` as the single opt-in switch; the path also requires Aiter, gfx950, and the GLM DSA model type.
- Cache bpreshuffled FP8 weights while retaining the original BF16 parameters for fallback, so enabled projections hold both copies.
- Fold q_b input quantization into the existing q/k RMSNorm in the active ROCm MHA/MLA forward paths. o_proj uses a standalone per-token quantization of the ROCm MLA attention output.
- Keep `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` on tuned Aiter BF16 for M≤512 and use PTPC FP8 for M>512; the threshold was selected empirically on MI355X. q_b_proj and o_proj use FP8 whenever the flag is enabled.
- Fall back to Triton quantization helpers on Aiter builds without the HIP fused per-token RMSNorm kernel.
- Add CPU unit coverage for the enablement gate, default-off BF16 behavior, weight repacking, PTPC dispatch, rollback, the M=512/513 boundary, and ROCm MHA/MLA routing.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4 MI355X, GSM8K (1319 examples):

| Validation | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| PTPC FP8 | 0.933 |

The result passes the accuracy acceptance threshold.

## Speed Benchmarks

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4 MI355X, 8k input / 1k output, three repetitions per concurrency on `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260921`. Both arms use validation commit `bb02414c4d22` and differ only by `SGLANG_DSA_FP8_PROJ_GEMM`.

A. BF16 — `SGLANG_DSA_FP8_PROJ_GEMM=0`:

| concurrency | TTFT (ms) | ITL (ms) | E2EL (ms) | output tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 1267.78 | 10.880 | 12516.31 | 327.05 |
| 8 | 2067.03 | 12.380 | 15440.83 | 530.44 |
| 16 | 3147.92 | 15.410 | 21249.94 | 770.99 |
| 32 | 6014.37 | 18.433 | 29752.64 | 1100.79 |
| 64 | 11327.56 | 24.157 | 46620.97 | 1406.28 |

B. PTPC FP8 — `SGLANG_DSA_FP8_PROJ_GEMM=1` (Δ vs BF16):

| concurrency | TTFT (ms) | Δ | ITL (ms) | Δ | E2EL (ms) | Δ | output tok/s | Δ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 1198.74 | −5.45% | 10.683 | −1.81% | 12246.82 | −2.15% | 334.33 | +2.23% |
| 8 | 1794.71 | −13.17% | 12.243 | −1.11% | 15128.43 | −2.02% | 540.76 | +1.95% |
| 16 | 2990.64 | −5.00% | 15.097 | −2.03% | 20661.20 | −2.77% | 792.74 | +2.82% |
| 32 | 5707.74 | −5.10% | 18.023 | −2.22% | 28825.35 | −3.12% | 1137.01 | +3.29% |
| 64 | 10813.16 | −4.54% | 23.840 | −1.31% | 45010.19 | −3.45% | 1456.26 | +3.55% |

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body: Currently working on another optimization that might be bundled into this one.
Due to CI maintenance mode, we need to merge main to run CI.

@Jacob0226 Addressed the ROCm forward split in `97493cf892`:

- moved q_b PTPC RMSNorm+quant dispatch into `forward_mha_rocm.py` and `forward_mla_rocm.py`
- moved MLA o_proj PTPC input quantization into `forward_absorb_rocm_core`
- removed the dead ROCm PTPC branches from the shared MHA/MLA prepare/core paths
- added focused ROCm routing coverage; 9/9 PTPC unit tests pass

Re-ran the full i8k/o1k TP4 A/B on MI355X with `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260921`, validation commit `bb02414c4d22`. The PR body now contains the refreshed latency and throughput tables.

NV CI passed except the known error from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/17050
CI error is from `/actions-runner/_work/sglang/sglang/test/registered/lora/test_multi_lora_backend.py`

> test_multi_lora_backend.py — AssertionError: ROUGE-L score 0.9773755656108598 below tolerance 1.0

Required checks failed on 93f622b; this PR cannot be merged until they pass.

**PR title** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39160991758))
> PR title must use "[Type] scope: title" or "[Type] [Hardware] scope: title". Type must be one of: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, Chore. Scope is required and may be any module or model name, with unrestricted letter case (letters, numbers, dots, underscores, slashes, or hyphens). Hardware is optional; use a single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend. Reverts must use GitHub's default format: Revert "original title". Use one space between fields and after the colon, with a non-empty title and no leading or trailing whitespace. Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
Edit the title; the check reruns on its own.

Since [#31531](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31531) landed, ROCm is dispatched to MLA_ROCM / MHA_ONE_SHOT_ROCM via resolve_rocm_forward_method, and this branch already includes that change. As a result, forward_absorb_prepare/core and forward_normal_prepare in the shared files are no longer reached on ROCm, so the q_b_proj RMSNorm+PTPC fusion added there doesn't take effect. The PTPC GEMM still runs through apply(), but after a BF16 RMSNorm and a standalone quant. I guess the perf numbers in the description were collected before the split, so the current branch may no longer reproduce them.
Once the changes are moved into the _rocm.py files, could you re-run the benchmark on the current branch and update the numbers?

+    @staticmethod
+    def _repack_bf16_to_fp8_ptpc(layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        """Keep the BF16 parameter and cache a shuffled PTPC FP8 weight copy."""
+        import aiter
+        from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_weight
+
+        weight = layer.weight.data
+        if weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16 or weight.dim() != 2:
+            return
+
+        fp8_weight, weight_scale = aiter.pertoken_quant(
+            weight, quant_dtype=aiter.dtypes.fp8
+        )
+        fp8_weight = shuffle_weight(fp8_weight, (16, 16))
+        layer._fp8_proj_weight = fp8_weight.contiguous()
+        layer._fp8_proj_weight_scale = weight_scale.contiguous()
+        layer._fp8_proj_ready = True
+

+            bf16_max_m = getattr(layer, "_fp8_proj_gemm_bf16_max_m", 0)

+            )

+

+                    layer._fp8_proj_weight_scale,
+                    bias=bias,
+                )

+        self.assertIs(actual_o_input, expected_o_input)
+        flatten_quant.assert_called_once()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main(verbosity=3)

reviews.body:
Since [#31531](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31531) landed, ROCm is dispatched to MLA_ROCM / MHA_ONE_SHOT_ROCM via resolve_rocm_forward_method, and this branch already includes that change. As a result, forward_absorb_prepare/core and forward_normal_prepare in the shared files are no longer reached on ROCm, so the q_b_proj RMSNorm+PTPC fusion added there doesn't take effect. The PTPC GEMM still runs through apply(), but after a BF16 RMSNorm and a standalone quant. I guess the perf numbers in the description were collected before the split, so the current branch may no longer reproduce them.
Once the changes are moved into the _rocm.py files, could you re-run the benchmark on the current branch and update the numbers?
